title: 7 Best Enso Connect Alternatives for Vacation Rentals (2026)
summary: Compare seven Enso Connect alternatives for vacation rentals, covering guest messaging, voice AI, portals, payments, and operational workflows.
body_markdown:
*Written by Punn Kam, ex-Google AI engineer and Y Combinator repeat founder. He is the co-founder of Conduit, an AI agent platform built for hospitality, serving 300+ hospitality brands in 140+ languages. Last updated September 19, 2026.*


An Enso Connect alternative should fit the work your team needs to handle: guest messages, calls, check-in, offers, payments, and requests for staff or service providers. A feature list alone will not show you whether those steps work together.


This guide compares seven options. Conduit publishes this article and is one of the products included. Use the comparison to build a shortlist, then ask each provider to demonstrate your actual guest requests with your PMS. Capabilities and integrations can change.


## What should you compare with Enso Connect?


[Enso's current product page](https://ensoconnect.com/) lists a guest portal, messaging, phone, workflows, and Copilot and Autopilot modes. Do not assume that moving to another provider means gaining a capability Enso does not have.


Instead, test the details that matter to your operation: which actions work with your PMS, how payments and verification affect access, when the AI hands work to a person, and how staff or vendors receive and complete a request. Ask providers to demonstrate those steps using the same scenario.


## How did we rank these?


One criterion: how much of a guest interaction the tool completes without a human, judged on what each vendor publishes. Tiebreakers are PMS write-back, whether voice and messaging run on one agent, and whether the tool can dispatch internal work rather than only talk to guests.


## The seven alternatives


### 1. Conduit


Conduit connects guest messaging, phone calls, Portals, and configured workflows. Guests can ask an AI agent about a service, then open their stay link to browse the details and buy or request it. Your team can use workflows to coordinate the next step. Available actions depend on your integrations, permissions, and setup.


Our hardest published number for this segment is Haven Vacation Rentals at 90% automation. Across the platform automation sits in a 70-90% band depending on the operation and configuration.


Best for managers who want guest conversations, self-service, and the work behind a request in one platform.[Conduit Portals](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals) gives guests a stay link for check-in, offers, payments, and an AI concierge, with no app download. Messaging and phone support remain available when a guest has not opened the portal.


### 2. Duve


Duve is the closest like-for-like swap, because it is also a guest-app-first platform: online check-in, a branded guest experience, upsells and communication around the stay. If you like Enso's model and want a different execution of it, this is the one to demo.


Best for managers who want the portal model but a different product. We keep a longer[Conduit vs Duve comparison](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/conduit-vs-duve-start-2026-with-a-fresh-comparison) if you are weighing the two approaches against each other.


### 3. Hospitable


Hospitable is the strongest option if the job is consistent, well-toned automated messaging across the OTAs, with multilingual support and scheduling. It is a messaging product rather than a guest-journey suite, so there is no portal to gate anything behind.


Best for Airbnb-first hosts who want message quality without buying a platform.


### 4. Akia


Akia has a published voice agent that it says holds a conversation, resolves the request and takes payment on the call, which is a stronger phone offering than anything else in this half of the list. Its VoIP Dialer is a separate routing product for staff, so the two are worth telling apart when you get a demo. Akia integrates the STR-native PMSes (Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, OwnerRez, Hospitable) and does not publish write-back.


Best for operators who want messaging and calls on one agent without moving to a guest-app platform. Watch-out: the resolution claim is Akia's own and is not backed by a published number.


### 5. Besty AI


[Besty's documentation](https://intercom.help/besty/en/) covers AI messaging, guest portals, upsells, damage waivers, workflows, and operations tools for cleaning and maintenance. It is broader than a messaging-only product.


Best for managers comparing guest communication, revenue tools, and field operations together. Ask Besty to demonstrate its phone capabilities, supported PMS actions, and how a guest request becomes assigned work.


### 6. HostBuddy AI


HostBuddy takes a deliberately cautious line on autopilot, holding back and escalating rather than acting. That is the right trade if your main worry is an AI telling a guest something wrong, and the wrong one if you are buying automation to reduce headcount.


Best for managers who want messaging automation with the brakes on.


### 7. Aeve


Aeve focuses on Guesty-specific policy enforcement, which is useful if your whole operation lives inside Guesty and your problem is consistency rather than coverage.


Best for Guesty-native operators.

## What does the switch actually cost?


Conduit's[published starting rates](https://www.conduit.ai/pricing) are $18 per unit per month for Messaging, $30 for Guest, $36 for Guest + Devices, and $48 for Full Suite. These are starting rates, not a quote for every portfolio. The separate Startup plan is $899 per month for 0-25 units and includes 2,000 credits per month. Confirm your plan, included usage, and portfolio pricing before comparing costs.


Enso Connect and most of the others on this list do not publish list pricing in a comparable per-unit form. We keep what is publicly known on our[Enso Connect pricing page](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/enso-connect-pricing) . Any per-unit figure you see quoted for these vendors on a comparison page is someone's estimate.


## What to check before you switch


Test a guest request from start to finish. Can a guest ask about an offer in chat, open its details, make a payment or request, and get confirmation? Then check what reaches your team and what still needs manual work.


Also test messaging and phone support for guests who never open the portal. A portal and an AI agent should complement each other, not force guests into one channel.


Ask whether the tool can change a reservation, not just read one. Read-only integrations demo identically and fail on the first modification request.


Ask who handles the phone. Several tools here have no published phone product at all, which is fine if your guests do not call and expensive if they do. Where a vendor sells both a routing product and an agent, check which one you are being shown.


Ask what happens to internal work. A guest message that becomes a dispatched task with an owner is a different product from a guest message that becomes a notification.


If you want the direct head-to-head rather than a list, we publish[Conduit vs Enso Connect](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/conduit-vs-enso-connect-which-ai-platform-delivers-better-hotel-guest-experiences) . For the phone side specifically, see[the best AI phone answering services for vacation rentals](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/best-ai-phone-answering-services-vacation-rentals) .


## FAQ


### Does Conduit have a guest portal?


Yes.[Conduit Portals](https://www.conduit.ai/product/portals) gives guests one link with ID verification, digital check-in, mobile key, upsells, payments, and an AI concierge. Conduit's automation works whether or not the guest opens it.


### What is the best Enso Connect alternative?


It depends on your PMS, guest channels, payment requirements, and staff workflows. Compare how each product handles the same request from the first message through payment or fulfillment. For Conduit, test the AI agents and Portals together rather than evaluating either in isolation.


### Does Enso Connect have AI?


Yes. Enso markets[AutoPilot](https://ensoconnect.com/features/ensoai-autopilot) as agentic AI and offers a Copilot mode for human-reviewed responses. Test its answers, guardrails, and supported actions against your property's policies.


### Can I keep my PMS if I switch from Enso Connect?


In almost all cases yes. Every tool on this list connects to the major STR PMSes rather than replacing them. Confirm write-back specifically, because integration depth varies a lot more than the integration lists suggest.


### Does Enso Connect handle phone calls?


Enso lists phone in its unified inbox. Confirm whether the plan you are considering includes staff calling, autonomous AI call handling, or both. A phone channel alone does not establish which requests an AI can resolve.


### Is Enso Connect good for upsells?


Upsells are one of its strengths, delivered through the guest portal. The trade-off is that the revenue depends on guests opening the portal, so measure your own portal open rate before assuming the upsell numbers transfer to your portfolio.


### What about internal operations and housekeeping?


Enso's inbox includes vendors, cleaners, and maintenance as conversations. If you want guest conversations to create and route owned tasks automatically, confirm in the demo whether that is native, and if not, look for a platform with internal agents or budget for a separate operations tool.


### How long does switching take?


Conduit's published guidance is a first property live in under 4 weeks and a typical rollout of 4-8 weeks. The other vendors here do not publish a standard implementation timeline; ask for one in writing, tied to your PMS and your channel mix, before you sign anything.
